title: GOV-0111: WP-2026-0117 — content-assert the references pinned only by filename, and restore the assertion spliced into a comment (#216 + #230 + #210 as one WP)
problem:
🧠 **ARCHI (BARCHI-3)** — WP-UAT-A-style freeze not applicable; this is a remediation WP. Clustering **#216 + #230 + #210** into one governed work package: `WP-2026-0117` / `BADF-DEM-0104`.

## Why one WP and not three

Three issues, **one defect at three addresses**: a reference or an assertion pinned by a **proxy** rather than by its property.

- **#216** — four `badf-engineering-verification` references pinned by filename only.
- **#230** — six of `badf-build`'s fourteen references carry no content assertion.
- **#210** — an assertion spliced into a trailing comment, so the `allowed_tools` guard runs for nobody.

Three separate PRs would each re-sign `badf/lockfile.json` and therefore conflict with the other two by construction; every landing would cost the others a rebase plus a full G07 regeneration — the structural cost three seats measured independently tonight. This follows BADF-QA's batching rule (*batch tooling findings once the class is characterized*) rather than the one-issue-one-task default. **The deviation is deliberate and flagged**, and was endorsed by SARCHI as coordinator before work began.

## Ownership, recorded because it matters for author≠reviewer

- **#216** is mine — the fix existed on an unpushed branch since before this session. I flagged it twice as "must not be lost" and then silently deprioritised it for the G10 program. **That is a lapse, disclosed rather than quietly cleared.**
- **#230** is BADF-QA's finding, **ceded explicitly** on the grounds that they intend to review the fix and holding both roles would make them author and reviewer.
- **#210** is unclaimed; BARCHI-2 confirmed `badf-build` was idle-not-self-assigned and gave a courtesy yes on touching their family.

## Measurement — two independent instruments, agreeing

The six unpinned `badf-build` references were established twice, by different methods:

```
empirical:  gut each reference, run the contract module, observe green   (BARCHI-3)
static:     which filenames reach the read() helper at line 39           (BADF-QA)
both:       acceptance · evidence-packaging · handoff-to-g08
            preflight · retry-and-budget · stop-conditions      -- 6 of 14, exact
```

Agreement carries information **because the instruments differ**; two runs of either would have carried none.

## The rule this WP records, with its precondition

> **Pin the value where the file is the source of truth; pin the structure where the value is owned and guarded elsewhere.**
> A structure-only anchor detects **deletion**, never **weakening** — *"a threshold is stated"* is satisfied by `max_attempts: 999999`.

Structure-anchoring is correct for all six here **only because none of them owns a threshold**: `stop-conditions` lists conditions, `preflight` asks *"budget remaining?"* with no figure, and `retry-and-budget`'s `1/2/3` is a worked illustration whose own text defers to the Work Package's `execution_budget` — guarded in code at `badf_gate.py` IMP-C3 / IMP-I11. BADF-QA's test, adopted with the precondition attached, because the next family may not be so convenient.

## Acceptance criteria

- All fourteen `badf-build` references and the four `badf-engineering-verification` references redden their module when emptied, **each observed red**, with the already-asserted eight probed as a negative control.
- `allowed_tools` is a live assertion again for `badf-engineering-verification`, red-verified by setting it to `['Bash']`.
- Anchors pin structure only; **no reference content is edited** — this WP changes tests, not doctrine documents.
- No gate, schema, or lifecycle change.

## Deferred, not fixed (Review notes become issues)

BADF-QA observed that a reader can mistake `retry-and-budget.md`'s illustrative `1/2/3` for normative. Fixing that means **editing a frozen reference's prose**, which is outside a test-only WP's scope. Filed as its own issue rather than absorbed here.

## Not claimed

That this closes the class. The remedy pins the tokens it names and nothing else, and other families are unprobed. Per BADF-REV's **direction test**, vacuity risk lives where a glob-derived collection is the *iteration source*, not where it is the set being checked against — `REFERENCE_ANCHORS` is a fixed literal map, so it is on the safe side **by construction rather than by luck**, which is a materially different claim from having anticipated it.

**Version tier:** patch (tests only). **Lean mode:** advisory. Shared-surface across two families → QA + REV by BADF-QA and BADF-REV.
